IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: Customer reachability alert for ACME (vpn-acme-01) — increased packet loss and BGP route flapping observed between us-east-2a and us-east-2b. Severity: P1. Pager duty @oncall. Links: https://monitoring.example.com/incident/3555551234 :pager:

Ashley: On it. I'm pulling the BGP adj/routing table and asking ACME if they see anything on their side.

Raj: I see flaps on the DirectConnect path and one of the VPN tunnels is dropping. BGP shows rapid withdraws for prefixes: 10.10.0.0/16.

Raj: Logs:
```
Mar 12 21:04:10 bgpd[1234]: Withdraw prefix 10.10.0.0/16 from peer dx-eus2-01
Mar 12 21:04:11 bgpd[1234]: Update with next-hop 192.0.2.5 for 10.10.0.0/16 from peer vpn-acme-01
Mar 12 21:05:02 bgpd[1234]: Peer vpn-acme-01 is down: hold timer expired
```

Lucy: Running `traceroute` from edge-eus2a to ACME's egress shows intermittent 100ms+ hops and packet loss starting at asn-64512. Might be an ECMP asymmetry.

Ashley: Can we fail traffic to the backup DX path for this customer? We have reserved backup via dx-eus2-b. If we can steer, we should reduce customer impact.

Raj: Preparing BGP policy change now — will announce preferred local-preference to dx-eus2-b for ACME prefixes. Applying in 30s.

IncidentBot: Deploy job queued by Raj (job id: 8792).

Lucy: Applied localpref 200 to dx-eus2-b, withdrawing preference on dx-eus2-a. Monitoring route propagation.

ACME Ops: Thanks for the heads up — we see traffic improve on our side around 21:08 UTC but some queries still timeout. We're running config checks.

Raj: Route propagation looks good, most prefixes now via dx-eus2-b. Some peers still show intermittent withdraws — possibly due to intermediate provider flap.

Carol: Reached out to carrier NOC (ticket #CN-5543) to request investigation of transitive circuit between us-east-2b and partner AS. Asked for ETA.

Ashley: Customer impact summary for postmortem: intermittent reachability for ACME between 21:03–21:12 UTC, elevated packet loss and request timeouts for ~20% of connections. No data plane encryption failures.

Oncall-Night: I'm taking the next shift handoff at 21:30 UTC. Current mitigation: traffic routed to backup DX path (dx-eus2-b). Carrier is investigating. Customer reports partial recovery. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if withdraws resume.

Carol: Carrier responded — possible intermittent fiber regen work causing microbursts, NOC assigned a field crew, ETA 45m.

Ashley: Added incident tags and created follow-up runbook actions: (1) track carrier field work, (2) validate BGP stability after crew completes, (3) run regression test suite against ACME prefixes.

Raj: Leaving a sticky note in routing config: revert localpref after carrier confirms stable route for 30m.

ACME Ops: Appreciated — will keep our ops team looped. No customer-facing outage page needed for now, but we'll update customers if ETA slips. :thumbsup:

Oncall-Night: Handoff complete. If any withdraws >3/min for >5m, page SRE lead. Otherwise will close once stable for 1h. :eyes:
